title: Arvutimuuseum: Computer Museum in Estonia
content:
Arvutimuuseum: Computer Museum in Estonia

Today I dropped by the Arvutimuuseum, the Computer Museum in Estonia. Such a nostalgic trip through the history of computing — from Soviet-era machines to quirky devices that once shaped (and sometimes failed) the future of tech. 🚀


📖 A Soviet-era computer book.


🍏 A whole wall of old Macs. Apple always had a style.






🐭 Apple mice — beautiful, but not always practical. Seems like "form over function" isn’t new for them.


💡 ZX Spectrum — proof that Raspberry Pi’s keyboard PC wasn’t the first “all-in-one” idea.


🧵 Magnetic core memory.


📇 Punch cards — programming with patience.



⌨️ Keyboards weren’t always QWERTY.


💻 Eee PC — one of my old favorites (alongside VAIO P). Both were defeated by the iPad revolution.



📱 Speaking of iPad, here’s the Apple Newton.


📟 PDAs everywhere — Palm, Psion, and more.


⌨️ A Palm foldable keyboard.


💿 Ubuntu once mailed you CDs for free. I still have mine.


🖊️ A mouse designed like a stylus — not the first attempt either.


📀 Storage evolution — floppy, cassette, CD-ROM.


💾 The original Save button.



🖥️ Old servers.


🇪🇪 Estonian-made computers!


🖨️ Printers & monitors powered by serial ports.


🧮 Calculators.


🎨 Early graphic computers.


🪟 Windows Chicago — no taskbar at first.



💼 The earliest laptops, one even had a built-in printer.



🚀 Space laptops — chips specially adjusted for space environments.


🇰🇷 Surprised to see Samsung personal computers that early — and wow, the screens were already impressive.


Such a fun dive into tech history. Every piece felt like a step that led us to the devices we casually use today. 🖥️📱💿
